q: 1. The property of the ingredients to separate from each other while placing the concrete is called ...........
explain: Segregation is the separation of constituent materials of concrete, usually resulting in the coarse aggregate settling or separating from the matrix.

q: 2. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness of R.C.C. footing on soils at its edges is kept not less than ...........
explain: To ensure durability and proper cover, IS:456 specifies a minimum edge thickness of 150 mm for footings on soil.

q: 3. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness at the edge on top of piles for a footing on the piles should not be less than ...........
explain: For footings on piles, the minimum edge thickness is increased to 300 mm due to the higher concentrated loads from piles.

q: 4. If the width of the foundation for two columns is restricted, the shape of the footing generally adopted is ...........
explain: A trapezoidal combined footing is used when the load of one column is much higher than the other and the width of the footing is restricted.

q: 5. In a combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment will occur ...........
explain: In combined footings, the shear force diagram typically crosses zero (maximum moment) near the heavier load point.

q: 6. A raft foundation is provided if the areas of the foundation exceeds the plan area of the building by ...........
explain: If individual footings cover more than 50% of the building area, a raft (mat) foundation is usually more economical and safer.

q: 7. Pile foundations are normally used ...........
options: when the bearing area require is not available
explain: Piles are used when surface soil is weak or when the space is too limited to provide a large shallow foundation.

q: 8. Pile foundations are invariably used in ...........
explain: Due to high water tables and heavy structural loads, bridge piers almost always utilize pile foundations for stability.

q: 9. A foundation rests on ...........
explain: Subgrade and foundation soil are terms used to describe the natural or prepared ground that supports the foundation load.

q: 10. For a number of columns constructed in a row, the type of foundation provided, is ...........
explain: A strip footing is a continuous foundation used to support a row of columns or a wall.

q: 11. To ensure uniform pressure distribution, the thickness of the foundation, is ...........
explain: Varying the thickness (as in sloped or stepped footings) helps distribute the stiffness and pressure more effectively.

q: 12. The self-weight of the footing is ...........
options: not considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
also considered for calculating the upward pressure on footing
not considered for calculating the area of the footing
explain: Self-weight acts downwards and is counteracted directly by the soil, so it is not included in the 'net' upward pressure used for designing the concrete section.

q: 13. Ina combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment occurs at ...........
options: a point equidistant from either column
a point of the maximum shear force
a point of zero shear force
explain: From basic mechanics, the maximum bending moment (hogging or sagging) always occurs where the shear force is zero.

q: 14. Top bars are extended to the projecting parts of the combined footing of two columns L distance apart for a distance ...........
options: 0.1 L from the outer edge of column
0.1 L from the centre edge of column
explain: This detailing rule ensures that top reinforcement (for hogging moments) is properly anchored into the cantilever projection.

q: 15. In general the formula for short terms deflection at the mid span can be expressed as ...........
explain: Standard deflection formulas for beams under distributed loads are proportional to $W \cdot L^4$ (or $P \cdot L^3$ for point loads).

q: 16. As per I.S. 456: 2000, the vertical deflection limits in a cantilever beam may generally be assumed to be satisfied provided that (span/depth) ratio does not exceed ...........
explain: To control deflection, IS 456 specifies basic span-to-effective-depth ratios: 7 for cantilevers, 20 for simply supported, and 26 for continuous beams.

q: 17. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of the same size should be less than ............
explain: To ensure proper concrete flow and bonding, the horizontal spacing between parallel bars should be at least equal to the diameter of the bar (or the maximum size of coarse aggregate plus 5mm).

q: 18. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of different size should not be less than ............
options: twice the diameter of thinner bar
explain: When bars of different diameters are used, the horizontal spacing must not be less than the diameter of the larger/thicker bar.

q: 19. The minimum thickness of the cover at the end of a reinforcing bar should not be less than twice the diameter of the bar subject to a minimum of ............
explain: For end cover of reinforcing bars, the rule is $2 \phi$ or 15 mm, whichever is greater, to protect the bar ends from corrosion.

q: 20. The centre to centre spacing of vertical stirrups, in a rectangular beam, is ............
explain: Shear force is maximum at the supports and minimum at the center. Therefore, stirrups are placed closer together at the ends and the spacing is increased toward the center.

q: 21. The spacing of vertical stirrups in a rectangular beam is ............
explain: Since shear force is highest at supports, stirrups are needed most there, resulting in the minimum (closest) spacing.

q: 22. The maximum spacing of vertical reinforcement in R.C.C. wall should not exceed the thickness of wall
explain: As per standard practice for reinforced concrete walls, the spacing of vertical reinforcement should not exceed 3 times the wall thickness or 450mm, whichever is smaller.

q: 23. A T-beam behaves like a rectangular beam of width equal to its flange, if neutral axis
explain: When the neutral axis is within the flange, the entire compression zone is rectangular (width = Bf). Since concrete in tension is ignored, the shape of the web doesn't affect the stress calculation.

q: 24. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: at the bottom edge of the slab
explain: If the compression zone (neutral axis) is contained entirely within the top flange, the calculation is identical to that of a rectangular beam of flange width.

q: 25. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: coincides the geometrical centre of the beam
explain: This is a repetition of the principle in Q229; as long as the NA is in the flange, it behaves as a rectangular beam.

q: 26. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. cantilever members is placed at
explain: In a cantilever beam, tension occurs at the top because it bends downward (hogging moment). Therefore, main reinforcement must be at the top.

q: 27. The main reinforcement in R.C.C simply supported member is placed at
explain: A simply supported beam under gravity loads experiences sagging (tension at the bottom), so reinforcement is placed in the bottom fibre.

q: 28. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. continuous members is placed at
explain: Continuous beams experience sagging (bottom tension) in the span and hogging (top tension) at the supports, requiring reinforcement at both top and bottom.

q: 29. The aspect ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: length to breadth of a slab
effective width of flange and effective depth of the beam
width of web and depth of flange
explain: Aspect ratio (ly/lx) is the ratio of the longer span to the shorter span of a slab, used to determine if it is one-way or two-way.

q: 30. The slab forming the top part of flanged the beam mid span in subject to compression over a length
options: greater than the width of the rib
equal to the width of the rib
less than the width of the rib
equal to the perimeter of effective rectangular of the section
explain: In flanged beams (T-beams), a portion of the slab (the flange) acts with the rib to resist compression, making the compression width much larger than the rib width.

q: 31. At continuous supports, the lower portion of
options: the slab experience neither the tension nor compression
explain: At supports of a continuous beam, hogging occurs. This means the top is in tension and the bottom (lower portion) is in compression.

q: 32. The intermediate beams between several beams case monolithically with the slab
explain: Beams cast monolithically with a slab act as T-beams when they have slabs on both sides (intermediate) and L-beams on the ends.

q: 33. Thickness of slab is taken
explain: While slab thickness varies, in the context of flanged beam design trials, df is often taken around 0.25d or the actual slab thickness.

q: 34. When the ratio of the long to short dimensions of the slab in greater than X, the slab may be designed as one-way slab where X is
explain: If Ly/Lx > 2.0, the slab primarily bends in the shorter direction and is designed as a one-way slab.

q: 35. The minimum percentage of high yield strength deformed reinforcement bars (H.Y.S.D.) provided in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: For HYSD bars, the minimum reinforcement is 0.12% of the gross area. (For mild steel, it is 0.15%).

q: 36. The maximum diameter of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum diameter of reinforcing bars shall not exceed 1/8th of the total thickness of the slab.

q: 37. The analysis of slab spanning is one direction is done by assuming it to be a beam of
explain: One-way slabs are designed as a series of 1-meter wide rectangular beams.

q: 38. The purpose of transverse reinforcement, in a slab, is to
options: distribute the effects of point load on the slab more evenly and uniformly
distribute the shrinkage and temperature cracks more evenly
keep the main reinforcement is position
explain: Transverse (distribution) steel handles temperature changes, shrinkage, and aids in load distribution.

q: 39. In a slab, the transverse reinforcement is provided at... to the span of the slab
explain: Transverse reinforcement is placed perpendicular (90 degrees) to the main span reinforcement.

q: 40. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the deflection of reinforced concrete slab or beam, for the purpose of design, is limited to... of span
explain: The span/250 limit is equivalent to 0.4%, but the question refers to the 1978 version where specific limits for finishes were set at 0.25% (span/400).

q: 41. A reinforced concrete slab is 75 mm thick. The maximum size of reinforcement bar that can be used is
explain: Max diameter = Thickness / 8 = 75 / 8 = 9.375 mm. The standard bar size below this is 8 mm.

q: 42. The shrinkage in a concrete slab
explain: As concrete dries, it shrinks. If restrained, this shrinkage develops internal tensile stresses, leading to tension cracks.

q: 43. The diameter of bars for main reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Main bars in slabs are typically between 8mm and 14mm. Bars smaller than 8mm are usually only used for distribution.

q: 44. The diameter of bars used for distribution reinforcement in slabs, may vary from
explain: Distribution or temperature bars are typically smaller, ranging from 6mm to 8mm.

q: 45. In a simply supported slab, alternate bars are curtailed at
explain: In simply supported slabs, bending moment reduces towards the ends, so bars are often cranked or curtailed at L/7 from the center of the support.

q: 46. According to Grashoff-Rankine theory, for a two-way slab which of the following holds true
explain: The theory states that load distribution is proportional to the inverse of the spans to the 4th power.

q: 47. For a slab spanning in two directions, the ratio of span to the depth of slab should not exceed
explain: For two-way slabs simply supported, the span/depth ratio limit is 35 (using Fe 250) or 28 (using Fe 415).

q: 48. In case of two-way slab, the limiting deflection of the slab is
options: primarily a function of the long span
primarily a function of the short span
independent of long or short spans
dependent on both long and short spans
explain: Deflection control for two-way slabs is based on the shorter span because it is the stiffer direction that carries more load.

q: 49. If the sides of a slab simply supported on its edges and spanning in two ways are equal, then the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab, the load is shared equally, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way span of the same length.

q: 50. The drop are provided in flat slabs to resist
explain: Drops (thickened portions of the slab) are primarily provided to increase the slab's resistance to punching shear at the column connection.
